# Workspace storage

Product workspaces use task state v4, managed basis v3, overlay identity v3 and SPM2 metadata. Each task binds to an immutable Git commit, Plastic changeset or managed NTFS directory. The mount combines the basis with the task's private ranges and metadata. A read resolves uncovered ranges from the basis. A partial write stores changed bytes. Original and peer edits stay isolated.

## Source journal and generated files

The product source journal uses an SJS1 control root and raw SJR2 segments. Segments roll at 16 MiB or 4,096 frames. These bounds apply to a unit of processing. Private extents, truncation, deletion, renames and metadata collectively describe the current tree. Source writes accepted into a durable journal batch share a flush and retain their ordering and individual outcome. Capture first drains pending kernel writes and fixes the exact source sequence. [Kernel flush and recovery](kernel-recovery.md)

In a Git or Plastic workspace, configured generated paths such as Unity's `Library`, `Temp` and `Logs` use a disposable partition. Tracked source takes precedence over generated-path patterns. Unchanged generated bytes read from the shared basis. Private edits use scratch files and ranges, with buffered I/O on the live path. A cross-partition rename stages and verifies the destination before replacement, records the participating identities and preserves open handles. Recovery checks those identities before completing an interrupted move. [Library basis](git-library-reference.md)

## Metadata and fixed results

Immutable metadata pages (up to 64 KiB), interned path components, per-directory indices, external sort and root-bound cursors allow consumers to work in bounded batches. Cache and batch limits apply to individual components. Native locks, runtime buffers, external clients and Unity Editors also contribute to process memory.

An intermediate checkpoint fixes a result while the same workspace continues. The generation binds the accepted source seal, reference inventory, private ranges and their physical backing. Native identity, content hashes and page checks are verified as required by the operation. Original publication locks the full target set and checks conflicts and per-path applied history before installation. [Publication and retry](repeated-original-apply.md)

## Maintenance and reclamation

Read histories and selections with `workspace read` using the returned root and cursor. For `workspace maintain`, retain the workspace, request key and scope. Resume pending collection, index copy or repack with that identity before starting another operation. An open reader can defer reclamation. A completed retry returns its receipt.

Release checks the fixed results, exact owned provider exit, before/after seals and the complete on-disk deletion inventory. Shared bases and payloads remain available to other readers. An unrecognized file, damaged proof or ownership mismatch stops destructive work. [Scale and fault qualification](plans/scalable-storage.md)
